title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-05
source: 7 Inch Half Track Reel Master @ 7.5 ips(Recorded In Venue By Bear on a Sony 770 Reel 2 Reel)-1st Generation Cassettes Transferred By Dick Latvala(Master Reel Playback on a Technics 1506 Reel 2 Reel-Tascam 122 MK111 Cassette Deck no Dolby); Analog to Digital Transfer(Cassettes played back on Nakamichi Dragon-Sony PCM-R500 DAT @ 44.1KHz by Jim Wise circa late 1990's); Zero Gen DAT play back on a Sony PCM R-500-Digital Out @ 16/44.1kHz-Digital Audio Labs Card deluxe-WAV @ 16/44.1KHz; Editing(Adobe Audition CC)-Mastering & Processing(iZotope Ozone 6)-FLAC encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name) JW:February 2015

ai_review.summary: Excellent mic‑sourced recording capturing a high‑energy set with standout St. Stephen, acoustic I Know You Rider and an intense Other One despite some monitor hiccups.
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its powerful performances – especially the acoustic “I Know You Riders,” a scorching St. Stephen jam and a fiery Other One that pushes the band to the edge of sonic overload.  The source is a stage‑mic (matrix‑like) capture; it’s remarkably clear and well‑separated, though listeners note occasional drum boominess, monitor feedback and a brutal cut on Cryptical Envelopment.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both performance and sound quality across multiple detailed reviews; minor technical quirks do not detract from overall excellence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stage‑mic capture with slight speaker boominess and drums a bit loud, occasional high‑pitched feedback on The Other One, and a harsh cut at the end of Cryptical Envelopment; overall very detailed, clean mix with good instrument separation.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows with high energy, moving from an intimate acoustic moment into a blistering St. Stephen and a chaotic Other One; despite monitor issues the band stays focused and the performance feels like it’s riding the edge of overload.

band_member_comments.Bob: Bob (referred to as "Bobby") is heard shouting “GODDAMMIT!” during The Other One, adding raw intensity.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums are noted as being mic'd too loud and contributing to a slight boominess in the mix.
